question.prompt: In an experiment, a scientific constant \(C\) is determined to be \(2.43865\) with an error of at most \(\pm0.00312.\) The experimenter wishes to announce a value for \(C\) in which every digit is significant. That is, whatever \(C\) is, the announced value must be the correct result when \(C\) is rounded to that number of digits. The most accurate value the experimenter can announce for \(C\) is

solutions.explanation:
The announced value must be the same rounded result for every value allowed by the error bound. Those possible values satisfy
\[
2.43865-0.00312\le C\le2.43865+0.00312,
\]
so
\[
2.43553\le C\le2.44177.
\]
This entire interval lies strictly between \(2.435\) and \(2.445\), the rounding boundaries for \(2.44\) to the nearest hundredth. Thus every possible \(C\) rounds to \(2.44\), which has three significant digits.

At the next precision, the allowed endpoints round to \(2.436\) and \(2.442\), so four significant digits are not guaranteed. Finer precision cannot work either: the possible values span \(0.00624\), while an interval rounding to a single thousandth or finer value has width at most \(0.001\). The most accurate guaranteed announcement is therefore \(2.44\), choice D.
solutions.title: Compare the uncertainty with rounding boundaries
